previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a right thigh abscess following two weeks of worsening pain, erythema, and swelling, accompanied by subjective fevers. She has a complex medical history including ESRD s/p deceased donor transplant, chronic immunosuppression, and prior MSSA infections. CT imaging revealed a large fluid collection in the anterior right thigh with hyperdense components, consistent with a superinfected resolving hematoma, not extending to deeper structures or the hip joint. She underwent bedside and OR incision and drainage, followed by wound VAC placement. Cultures grew MSSA, prompting a switch from vancomycin to cefazolin for renal safety. Her infection resolved with treatment, WBC normalized, and wound improved. She was managed for comorbidities including hypertension, diastolic heart failure, and CKD, with medication adjustments. Due to prior opioid-related respiratory depression, her pain regimen was simplified. She was discharged home with services for IV antibiotics, wound care, and follow-up, declining inpatient rehab despite recommendations.

Ms. ___ is a ___ w/ESRD s/p DDRT ___, ___, CAD, PAH, right

# Septic shock/Aspiration pneumonia: 
On ___, following intubation and aspiration, rapidly developed

pneumonia seems most likely, much less likely thigh abscess or 
UTI. Blood culture were negative. Wound culture from a 
sub-centimeter abscess grew coag+ staph, but was not thought to

which was also an unlikely cause. There was consideration of a 
possible intra-abdominal source given presenting symptoms, 
although CT torso to knees showed no obvious souce. TTE showing 
general hypokinesis, EF40%, with TR and MR, no vegetation. She 
was treated with vanco (___), linezolid (___), 
ceftazidime (___), metronidazole (___), tobramycin 
(___). She eventually grew E. coli in her sputum ___, 
sensitive to ceftazidime (other antibiotics discontinued and

with stress dose hydrocortisone. On ___ her pressor requirement 
began to decrease. By ___ she was off pressors. Lactate 
peaked at 5.5 and eventually trended to normal. 
 
# Hypoxemic/hypercarbic respiratory failure: 
Originally intubated for inadequate compensation of metabolic 
acidosis, however, developed severe ARDS, likely ___ to 
aspiration during intubation as well as sepsis. She was managed 
with lung protective ventilation guided by transpulmonary 
pressure targets using esophageal balloon measurements and early 
paralysis with cisatracurium. She improved over the next few 
days, passed SBT, RSBI 77, and was extubated on ___.

# Acute stroke: 
On ___, while under neuromuscular blockade, patient was noted 
to have anisocoria, L pupil 6mm and R pupil 2mm. Non-contrast 
head CT showed left temporoparietal stroke with edema. We 
consulted neurology. On their read there was also a right-sided 
watershed lesion. Both lesion were likely explained by 
hypotension rather than cardioembolus from AFib. Off sedation, 
formal neuro exam was at baseline. MRI was discussed with 
patient for further evaluation and for prognostic purposes; 
however, the patient declined to undergo any further imaging. In 
discussion with neurology, repeat head CT not felt to be useful.

# Atrial fibrillation: 
New onset afib in the setting of septic shock. Initial rate 
control was attempted with metoprolol, then diltiazem with poor 
response. Patient started on amiodarone, received 24-hour load 
on ___. Completed amiodarone 10g load on ___ and switched to 
200 mg PO daily maintenance dose. Patient reverted to NSR on 
___. Anticoagulation was held initially in setting of GI

discharge, but she declined to stay in the hospital for a
